note: Canonical dialogue (English source). FR dubbing is a SEPARATE human/translation step — NOT fabricated. Lines preserved verbatim; scenes/lines not found are flagged, never invented.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: She's pulling beam-on. I hold, she rolls. I fall off, I lose the next shoulder.

lines.speaker: OLAF
lines.text: And which does the water want?

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: I'm not asking what the water wants. I'm asking you to tell me I'm right.

lines.speaker: OLAF
lines.text: Ask the sea, Astrid. I've answered you for the last time tonight.

lines.speaker: TOVE
lines.text: When we drown, I'm telling the gods it was the navigator's nerves. Not the sea.

lines.speaker: HELGI
lines.text: Tell them what you like. She'll steer us true the second she stops waiting for the old man to blink first. Trouble is she's never once done it.

lines.speaker: TOVE
lines.text: She will. She has to. I've got a beach to get back to, Helgi. I'm not dying in a story nobody at home will even hear.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: ...I can't read that.

lines.speaker: HELGI
lines.text: THEN STEER LIKE HE'S ALREADY GONE —

lines.speaker: OLAF
lines.text: ...You didn't ask me.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: There wasn't time.

lines.speaker: OLAF
lines.text: No. There wasn't. Remember that it felt like that.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: We didn't cross to raid you. Your sea reached up and took us off ours.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: Whatever comes out of that sky, you do not touch it. Not this time.

lines.speaker: IPY
lines.text: You said that last time. Then the sea took the market.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: IPY — BACK —

lines.speaker: IPY
lines.text: You knew where it would go.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Yeah. I did.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: The sky tears, and the same morning strangers fall out of it. The people will want to know which caused which. Chain them.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: Commander — they came *through* the tear. The ghost-girl just pulled Ipy out of it.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: I did not ask what is true. I asked what the town needs to see while it is frightened. And it needs to see that I have the thing that smells the flood before it comes — on a leash. Bring them to the garrison. The sea-ghosts are mine.

lines.speaker: WIDOW
lines.text: I kept your place, Nahla. I keep telling them the sea took a corner, not a curse. You. Ghost. They say you smell the water before it comes. Then smell mine — tell me which morning it comes for the rest of us.

lines.speaker: ELDER
lines.text: Three markets drowned this season, Commander. The people say the gods are angry at something we have not punished.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: Then we will punish something. Strangers fell from the torn sky this morning. The gods could not have sent a clearer answer. Give them a guilty face to hate, and they will not notice the face that cannot stop the water.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: You read water. I have spent my life reading *that.*

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Then tell me how to make it give my father's ship back.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: It is an alignment — the two suns draw close, the wall between their ages thins, things fall through. The debt must be repaid, or both ages bleed together until neither keeps its own rules. It closes only when someone who can read it walks into it and shuts it from within. It does not return that someone.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: And if no one walks in?

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: Then the bleed grows until there is no shore left to argue it on. You are already asking the wrong question — *how do I use it* — instead of the right one: *what will it cost whoever does.*

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: Every name here could read the seam. Every name is also the one who shut it, the last time it tore wide. My teacher. I cut that myself, with this thumbnail, the morning after she didn't come back out of the light.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Thirty years learning a thing whose only prize for learning it is that it keeps you.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: I did not expect to meet someone who could read it better in a month than I in a life. I find I don't know whether I envy you the gift — or the blank plaster where your name isn't yet.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Where's the space for the next one?

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: There is always space for the next one. That is the whole cruelty of the wall.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: You have guarded that tear your whole life, Nefer-Ka, and it has never torn like this. Why now?

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: The alignment makes a seam possible. But this one opened wide, and early, before the suns had met. That is not the alignment. That is a hand.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: A hand. Whose?

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: The priests would know better than a river-captain, Commander.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: Find me the hand, guardian. A guilty hand is a gift — the people forgive a ruler anything if he gives them someone to blame. The foreigners will do until you find better.

lines.speaker: VIGGE
lines.text: My mother said one voyage and I'd come home a man. She didn't say which world I'd do it in.

lines.speaker: BÖRK
lines.text: You come home a man from any sea you don't drown in, lad. Even the ones made of sand, it seems.

lines.speaker: HELGI
lines.text: We all get home, Vigge. The navigator reads us a door. She has to. I've a girl who still thinks this horse is in my hand and not my belt.

lines.speaker: TOVE
lines.text: Then she'd better learn to want the door for herself, and fast. She only ever reads one when her father tells her she's allowed.

lines.speaker: OLAF
lines.text: When you were small you'd stand at the steerboard and call the weather before I did. Every time. And every time you'd look at me after, to see if you were allowed to be right.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: You were the captain.

lines.speaker: OLAF
lines.text: I was your father. That's worse. I heard the guardian. "From within." I saw your face find a route and hide it from me.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: If there's a way home in that light, I'll read it.

lines.speaker: OLAF
lines.text: Read it to get the crew home. Read it to get Helgi back to his girl and Tove to her beach. But if you ever walk into a thing you can't walk out of — let it be a choice you make, not a grave you dig for me. Promise me that much.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: ...Sleep, Father.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: My guardian says the tear widens and will drown my towns. You see where water will go. So you will walk the shore and keep my people dry, and I will not feed your crew to the thing to calm a mob. That is the whole of the kindness I have.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: And my father? My ship?

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: My guests. Under my roof. A man keeps his guests close when he wants a borrowed animal to come home at night.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: He keeps what you love so your gift stays his.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: I worked that out before he finished smiling. Teach me the light. That's the one thing he can't hold.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: I read it east. It went west. At home the sea never lied to me like that.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: The sea at home kept one set of rules. This keeps two, badly, and changes which mid-breath. You cannot read it the way you read a thing you trust. You have to read it the way you'd read a man who might betray you — watching for the moment it decides to.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: I've never trusted anything enough to watch it that close. Not without my father's eyes telling me I saw right.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: Then learn. His eyes are closing, and the light does not wait for a captain's nod.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: That one you didn't look at me after.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: ...No. I didn't.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: Two crews. One tide. Nobody lost.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Nobody lost. First time I've read the water and not had to count a cost when it drained.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: Hold that feeling close. The seam will come for it next.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: Your people sing about drowning a great deal.

lines.speaker: TOVE
lines.text: We sing about it so it doesn't happen. You sing about rivers so they stay in their banks. Same prayer, different water.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: That child lost her mother to the first tide. She laughs anyway. I don't know how she does it and I can't look straight at it.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: She looks at things straight. My father said keep her close. Why can't you look at her, Meryt?

lines.speaker: TOVE
lines.text: Halla asked me once what I'd do if the sea kept you instead of me. I laughed — said the sea's not fool enough to take the one who reads it. I've stopped laughing at that one.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: You'll see her. I'll read you to that beach myself.

lines.speaker: TOVE
lines.text: You've steered us across half the world and back through a hole in the sky, and you still asked a dying man on that deck whether you were allowed to be right. Why do you do that?

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Because if he says yes and I'm wrong, it was his call. If I choose, and I'm wrong —

lines.speaker: TOVE
lines.text: — then it's yours to carry. Aye. That's the price of the steering-oar. Nobody told me either when they handed it to me. You just find out you're holding it.

lines.speaker: IPY
lines.text: My mother sold sweet water there. The first morning the sea walked, it walked here. It took the corner. And her. I keep her place.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: My mother went to the sea too. Before I was old enough to carry a jug. I keep her place by reading the water she's in. You keep yours by standing on it.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: The east row — get them OFF it — NOW!

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: Your commander's foreign hounds smell the flood before it comes! Fear nothing while I hold their leash!

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Your commander holds no leash. The water answers the reading, and the reading is hers — — and mine. He stood where it was already safe. Ask him to stand where I say the next one breaks, and watch if he dares.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: She is more useful and more dangerous than I thought. Tighten the guard on the old man. A dangerous animal comes home faster when it fears for its master.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: It is not only leaking water now. It is leaking TIME. The two ages are forgetting which of their dead are dead. When the wall forgets enough, there is no 'before' left to send your father's ship home to. No shore to go back to at all.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: How long?

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: Days. Then the convergence chooses for us, whether we are ready or not.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: My guardian says the tear was forced open by a hand, and closes only when a life is given to it. I have decided the life will be a *guilty* one — the hand that opened it. The people will love the justice. You will read me and my guardian to the tear's root at the convergence. If your reading falters, or your crew grows brave, your father does not see another ugly double dawn.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: He means to find the guilty hand and feed it to the seam at the convergence. He thinks a guilty life closes it cleaner.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Does it? A guilty life?

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: It closes when someone who can *read* it shuts it from within. Guilt is Seth- Nakht's idea, not the seam's. But if he needs a guilty hand to throw, and mine is the guilty one — I could spare a great many people by being the hand.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: That's not a plan. That's your grief finally finding a door it's allowed to walk through.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: My brother. The river took him in flood — no body, no cairn, nothing to grieve but water. The morning of the turning I lit the dawn-rite as duty asks. And then I lit it a second time. For him. Forbidden. To beg the river back just once. The suns touched twice. The sky tore wide. Every corner the sea has taken since — Ipy's mother — I called it down trying to un- drown one man.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: And now you'd let a commander throw you in to make it even.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: Wouldn't you? If the drowning were yours to answer for?

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: I don't know yet. I think I'm about to find out what I'd walk into. But not for his theatre, Meryt. If anyone walks into that light, it won't be to settle your account for a man who wants a crowd.

lines.speaker: HELGI
lines.text: Sǫlveig lost the first horse I made her — dropped it off a jetty, cried a whole day. I carved the one in my belt that night and swore I'd set it in her hand myself. Spare. In case this world's as hard on a child's toys as the last one.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: You'll give her both yourself.

lines.speaker: HELGI
lines.text: If I don't — then you don't carry it to her out of guilt, Astrid. You carry it because you chose to. There's a difference, and your whole life you've only done the first kind — the duty, the nod, the thing you were told. Learn the second kind before the day you need it. Don't learn it the way I think you're about to.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: Walk only where I walk. Here the world has forgotten which age it stands in.

lines.speaker: TOVE
lines.text: If I die in this place I die owing a woman an explanation she's waited a year for. You're getting us to her. Say it.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: I'm going to get *you* to her, Tove. Her name first, so I know who I'm aiming you at.

lines.speaker: TOVE
lines.text: ...Halla. Of Hǫrn. She mends nets and she swore she'd never love a sailor and then she did it anyway, the fool. You said "you." Not "us."

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Mind the glass. Left of me.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: Even he gets shown what he's closest to losing. Watch him. A man who has just met the worst version of himself is a man who can still turn — or harden for good.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: OFF THE SADDLE — it floods the saddle — GO —

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: HELGI — drop the line — take my hand — REACH —

lines.speaker: HELGI
lines.text: Get her home — Sǫlv—

lines.speaker: TOVE
lines.text: He threw it to you. Not his own hand. Why —

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Because he'd already chosen who the horse was for. He stopped trying to save himself and saved the thing that mattered. I spent my whole life not understanding that. I understand it now.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: The hand was mine, Commander. My brother drowned; I lit the dawn-rite a second time, for him, forbidden. The suns touched twice. I tore the sky. Not these foreigners — me.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: My own captain. Even better — the people will see I spare no one, not even my own. Hold her for the tear. At the convergence, the guilty hand goes in. And you will read her safely to the heart, so my justice does not miss.

lines.speaker: IPY
lines.text: The first morning the sea walked. That was your second flame. My mother.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: ...Yes. Your mother. And every corner it took since. Me.

lines.speaker: IPY
lines.text: Seth-Nakht wants to throw you in. I don't. I want you to stand on the shore where she stood, every day, and not look away from it. That lasts longer than drowning.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: He has it wrong. The seam does not want guilt. It wants a reader, and it keeps them. If Meryt walks in, she dies for his story and the seam still needs a reader after. There are two people here who can read it to the heart. Her hand is not one of them.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Then he's about to spend the wrong life — and he'll keep spending them until he spends the right one. Unless someone reads it before he can stage his justice.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: At the joining of the suns, the guilty hand goes into the tear, and your commander closes the wound his own captain opened! Read her path to the heart. Now.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: If I walk her in, she dies and the seam stays open — she can't read it shut. You'll have spent a life for a story and you'll still be standing here when the next dawn doubles.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: Then I will spend another. I have a garrison of hands.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: You have two readers. Her, and me. Spend us and you have none — and no one to shut the tear the day it opens over your own house.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: There — NOW! *The sand UNDER the charging wedge erupts to sea mid-stride; three men go down thrashing, armour dragging them; one, SERGEANT KHAY, is pulled under to the chest before the water drains and drops him, coughing, onto dry dune — a real casualty of the ground, not a kill by her hand.*

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: Flank her! The rock's dry side —!

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: The dry side goes next. Step there and you drown. *A beat of terror holds the flankers — and then, by luck or by read, a thin tongue of sea licks the dry side and withdraws. The bluff holds. She's trembling now, soaked, voice cracking — reading at the edge of collapse, each call costing her more than the last.*

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: You never held the leash. I did. And I just showed your own men whose hand the water takes orders from.

lines.speaker: SETH-NAKHT
lines.text: HOLD THE LINE FOR THE FOREIGNERS. Hold it! ... Not a throne of sand. Not that.

lines.speaker: VIGGE
lines.text: BÖRK —

lines.speaker: TOVE
lines.text: He chose it. He chose you. Hold onto that, boy — out here it's all any of us gets to keep.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: The heart's there. Not where it's brightest — where it's quiet.

lines.speaker: NEFER-KA
lines.text: Thirty years. You found it on your first convergence.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: I never once trusted the water under my own feet. I'm done not trusting it. Your world needs a reader standing on this shore for the next tear — and the one after. That's you. It was always going to have to be you who stays, so it can't be you who goes.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: It should be me. I opened it. Let me be the one who —

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Your grief opened it. Your life won't close it — you can't read it, and I won't spend you on a commander's idea of justice. You don't get to drown your way out of this. You stand on the shore where it happened and you don't look away. That's longer, and it's yours. Guard it with him.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: I can send you all home through the seam before I shut it — the ship, Tove, the grey sea. Or I close it. Not both. The light keeps the reader who shuts it.

lines.speaker: OLAF
lines.text: The sea takes what it's owed, girl. Owe it me — not you. I spent your whole life being the eyes behind yours. Close it. Live on the far side. And say it out loud, once, so I hear you choose before I go.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: I'm closing the seam. I'm staying. You go home without me. I chose it. No one told me to.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Take him to the grey sea, Tove. Take the crew home. And this — — to Sǫlveig, from your hands, not mine. And Halla of Hǫrn: tell her you didn't drown. Tell her to her face. Don't make her read it in a story.

lines.speaker: TOVE
lines.text: I'll tell her you're the reason I got to. You said "you," not "us," in that canyon. I heard it then. Read your way to something good over here, Astrid. Promise me a thing, once, out loud, like you mean it.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: I promise I'll choose it. Whatever it is. Myself.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: I know. I know. But I didn't choose you. I'm choosing this.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: What do your people call a navigator with no sea left to cross?

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: We don't have a word for it. But that river runs further than anyone here has followed it. Someone should learn to read it.

lines.speaker: MERYT
lines.text: Further than anyone's dared.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Then it had better be me.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: See where it goes quiet, there, past the bar? That's where it's deepest. The loud water's shallow. It's the quiet you have to learn to read.

lines.speaker: IPY
lines.text: ...Like the seam. The heart was the quiet part.

lines.speaker: ASTRID
lines.text: Like the seam. Your turn. Read me the next bend. Don't look at me after to see if you're right. Just be right.
